purpose: minimum contract that would close GOV-SCOPE-001

minimum_properties.property: constructed exactly once per bound source entry
minimum_properties.detail: keyed by the warrant row identity: source_key + canonical_sha256 + format + operation plan. Constructing a second session for the same bound entry must be detectable, not silently permitted.

minimum_properties.property: owns the source path, identity, format, operation plan and budget
minimum_properties.detail: the operation plan is the per-source declaration of which operations are admitted (existence, hash, metadata, selected, full, chunk, header-prefix, retries) and which are not.
minimum_properties.closes: GOV-HDR-002 and the SRC08/SRC12 full-read hazard: the plan states that header-prefix is admitted only for SRC26 and that metadata-only classes forbid full reads

minimum_properties.detail: the session creates the single SourceAccessBroker, and every decode within the session reads through that one open. No nested or replacement broker.

minimum_properties.property: exact operation plan enforced BEFORE each operation
minimum_properties.detail: each admitted operation is gated by the session plan plus the budget; a non-admitted operation is refused pre-operation with a typed error at the outer boundary.
minimum_properties.preserves: the accepted bridge-safe refusal discipline (never raise through the pyreadstat read callback)

minimum_properties.property: decoder-entry counter with a pre-operation ceiling
minimum_properties.detail: decoder_invocations added to the account and budget, incremented once per governed decode entry, kept strictly separate from reader_invocations/full_reads/metadata_reads/chunk_reads.

minimum_properties.property: route-pass accounting distinct from lower layers
minimum_properties.detail: a route-pass account that records the outer governed pass and is never collapsed into full_reads, chunk_reads or reader_invocations; a second pass is refused where max=1.
one close path that is idempotent, plus a receipt aggregating every account over the whole source entry (not per-decode).

minimum_properties.property: second-session / second-decode refusal where budgets require it
minimum_properties.detail: when the frozen expectation is exactly one (SRC27 pass; SRC02/SRC06/SRC14 selected read), the second attempt must be refused with a typed error naming the exhausted account.
the session must never degrade to a raw path string or to an ungoverned read path; refusal, not fallback.

what_such_an_owner_still_would_NOT_solve.detail: an in-process session owner cannot by itself prevent a SECOND PROCESS or a restarted run from constructing its own first session. S8 refuses within a session; nothing in an owner object spans processes. A warrant-grade 'exactly one pass' guarantee therefore also requires an authority-held durable mechanism (e.g. an adopted event/marking record) or an operational control that a second run is not started. This must be stated rather than assumed.

the owner can AGGREGATE and ENFORCE a reader-byte ceiling but cannot INVENT one. No real-source numeric reader-byte ceiling is source-free frozen (HQ199 adjudication), and synthetic carrier totals are not warrant budgets. A source whose lawful requirement exceeds any chosen cap can only be refused, not completed.

reader_bytes scales with file size and format; a fixed numeric cap cannot be both safe for a large source and non-blocking for a small one without a size-derived rule. Deriving such a rule is an authority task, not an owner task.
the owner can REFUSE a header-prefix read for a class that does not admit one, but it cannot decide whether such a read should instead be re-admitted by amending the operation law. That is authority.

what_such_an_owner_still_would_NOT_solve.limitation: the authority question of whether decoding a source for metadata only constitutes a decoder invocation at all
what_such_an_owner_still_would_NOT_solve.detail: if a metadata-only admission is not a governed decode entry, SRC08/SRC12's decoder_invocations expectation must be stated explicitly; the owner enforces whatever is declared but cannot settle the declaration.
